item.title: China earmarks 80 mln yuan for Xizang quake relief, recovery efforts
item.description:

Sixteen people were killed and 65 others injured after a 7.0-magnitude earthquake struck Baqen County of Nagqu City in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region at 10:33 p.m. Thursday, the city's earthquake relief headquarters said on Friday. The Ministry of Emergency Management and authorities in Xizang have mobilized resources for rescue and relief operations. (Xinhua/Purbu Tsering) BEIJING, Oct. 23 (Xinhua) -- China has allocated 50 million yuan (about 7.5 million U.S. dollars) in emergency disaster relief funds and earmarked another 30 million yuan for recovery efforts following a 7.0-magnitude earthquake in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region. The earthquake struck Baqen County of the city of Nagqu at 10:33 p.m. on Thursday, leaving 16 people dead and 54 injured. The Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Emergency Management jointly allocated 50 million yuan to support rescue operations and assistance to affected residents, while the National Development and Reform Commission earmarked the additional 30 million yuan from the central budget to help restore damaged infrastructure and public service facilities. The country has also upgraded its national earthquake emergency response from Level IV to Level III, while activating a separate Level-IV national natural disaster relief response. China's national comprehensive fire and rescue force has dispatched a total of 350 rescuers and 83 vehicles for rescue operations. The emergency management ministry has guided Xizang's emergency management department in arranging for Wing Loong drone deployment to the quake-hit area for disaster reconnaissance. As of 6:30 a.m. on Friday, 120 rescuers and 27 vehicles had arrived in the quake-hit area, while the remaining 230 rescuers and 56 vehicles from the Xizang fire and rescue corps were en route as reinforcements, having all entered Nagqu's administrative area. Earlier, as of 4:30 a.m. on Friday, authorities had mobilized relief supplies at the central, regional, municipal and county levels, and delivered them in batches to the affected area. These supplies included 1,000 prefabricated housing units, 3,239 tents, 2,821 folding beds and 4,280 quilts, among other essentials. ■ An aerial drone photo taken on Oct. 23, 2026 shows a temporary shelter at an earthquake-hit village in Maru Township of Baqen County, Nagqu City, southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region. item.title: China's "city of the future" takes center stage at global governance talks
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-23
SHIJIAZHUANG, Oct. 23 (Xinhua) -- Xiongan New Area, China's "city of the future" built on the North China Plain, is drawing wide attention with the 2026 Global Governance Forum (Xiongan) scheduled to kick off there on Friday. The forum brings together leading figures in strategic affairs, politics, academia, business, media and youth affairs from around the world, particularly those working on issues related to the United Nations, climate change, artificial intelligence and multilateral trade. While the attendees discuss frontier topics ranging from climate change and AI governance to multilateral trade and sustainable urban development, the host city Xiongan, located in north China's Hebei Province, itself serves as a living laboratory for global governance, with hands-on experience in urban governance, green transition and digital governance. Located about 100 kilometers southwest of Beijing, the new city that is still taking shape has covered 222 square kilometers of developed urban area. Over 5,300 buildings have been completed, with a total floor area exceeding 62.14 million square meters. In April 2017, China decided to establish the Xiongan New Area as part of a strategy to promote the coordinated development of the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region. Serving as a hub to accommodate non-capital functions relocated from Beijing, the city was designed to be smart, green, innovative, livable, and free from "urban ills." DIGITAL CITY When it comes to digital governance, the Xiongan Urban Computing Center, notably, holds more than 40 billion high-quality data records. The city has built over 500 kilometers of smart roads, leveraging 5G technology for intelligent connected vehicle trials. The roads are equipped with lampposts that integrate traffic lights and various sensors. The computing center, with its facade reminiscent of the shape of an eye, is considered the city's "brain." On a huge electronic screen, real-time data show the city's operation in nearly every respect. Which road has more traffic? Anything unusual in the underground pipes? Are the neighborhood trash cans full? In Xiongan, every building has its digital model, and every pipe is fitted with sensors. Xiongan has been planned and built as three synchronized cities. Beyond the urban surface buildings, there is a city in the cyber cloud and another underground. Beneath the ground run utility tunnels. Water, electricity, gas and heating pipelines are all placed inside these tunnels, with reserved lanes for logistics. On Tuesday, China National Data Group Co., Ltd., a new state-owned enterprise (SOE) directly administered by the central government, was officially inaugurated in Xiongan. It is positioned as a national team for data services, a leader in data infrastructure connectivity, and a strategic force for national data sci-tech innovation. GREEN DEVELOPMENT Above ground, Xiongan is a garden city. Residents can reach a park within a 300-meter walk, and a woodland within three kilometers. Xiongan's urban development places the natural landscape at the heart of the city's design, laying a solid foundation for an eco-friendly future city to ensure quality of life. Since 2019, Xiongan has embarked on a comprehensive initiative to treat rural sewage, garbage and toilet waste in the vicinity of Baiyangdian Lake, one of northern China's major wetlands. Latest figures reveal that the city has completed 484,500 mu (roughly 32,300 hectares) of new afforestation, bringing its total green area to 744,500 mu and lifting its forest coverage rate to 35.2 percent. According to Xiongan's planning and construction bureau, green buildings account for 100 percent of new projects, with some achieving ultra-low energy consumption. ALLEVIATING BEIJING'S PRESSURE After nine years of construction, Xiongan has become a key hub for the relocation of Beijing's non-capital functions. Among these relocated projects, the headquarters of China Satellite Network Group Co., Ltd. operates steadily. Headquarters of Sinochem Holdings and China Huaneng Group Co., Ltd. have settled and begun regular operations in Xiongan. Also, China Mineral Resources Group Ltd. has seen the near completion of the main structure of its headquarters in the city. Four universities and several hospitals from Beijing, including Beijing Jiaotong University and Peking University People's Hospital, are under construction in Xiongan. To date, more than 400 branches of state-owned enterprises (SOEs) directly administered by the central government and over 600 high-tech firms have settled there. "The forum held in Xiongan builds an important platform to exchange urban governance ideas and share cutting-edge insights with the world," said Li Huaxia, head of the publicity, cyberspace affairs and information bureau of Xiongan New Area. By hosting this international forum, Xiongan is putting its capacity to the test, while demonstrating its pivotal role in the coordinated development of the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region and its unique geographic advantages. In terms of transport, it sits close to Beijing Daxing International Airport. A direct expressway opened in 2023 connecting Xiongan and this airport. Xiongan is just a 30-minute high-speed rail ride away from Beijing. Last month, China also opened a high-speed rail section connecting Xiongan with Shangqiu in central China's Henan Province. Noting that the Xiongan-Shangqiu section fills a gap in Xiongan's southbound high-speed rail corridor, Liu Yanhong, deputy general manager of Xiongan high-speed railway corporation, said the line facilitates commuting and business exchanges for relocated enterprises and institutions, and supports stronger industrial cooperation along the route. ■

item.title: Xiplomacy: Reading Xi's vision for global governance through metaphors
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-23
BEIJING, Oct. 23 (Xinhua) -- The 2026 Global Governance Forum (Xiong'an) is set to open on Friday in the Xiong'an New Area, north China's Hebei Province, bringing into world focus a pressing question: How can countries work together to address shared challenges in an interconnected world amid growing protectionism and unilateralism? In speeches and meetings on multiple occasions, Chinese President Xi Jinping has used vivid metaphors to articulate his vision for global governance. These metaphors offer insights into his approach to building a more just, equitable and inclusive global governance system. IN SAME BOAT "I was looking at the vast ocean when I boarded the ship, and it struck me that we are all indeed fellow passengers in the same boat," Xi said while addressing the 2018 APEC CEO Summit hosted at a unique setting -- onboard the giant cruise Pacific Explorer in Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea. The metaphor embodies the essence of Xi's vision of building a community with a shared future for humanity, highlighting the interconnectedness of countries and the need for solidarity and cooperation in addressing common challenges. Today, the interconnected world is grappling with four mounting deficits: a peace deficit that exacerbates geopolitical conflicts, a development deficit that widens the North-South divide, a security deficit that erodes mutual trust, and a governance deficit that undermines the effectiveness of multilateralism. In 2019, at the China-France Global Governance Forum held in Paris, Xi proposed a four-pronged approach to addressing the four deficits. First and foremost, he called for fairness and reasonableness to address the governance deficit. "It is advisable to uphold a vision of global governance featuring extensive consultation and joint contribution for shared benefits," Xi said, calling for actively advancing the democratization of global governance rules. As the world has found itself in a new period of turbulence and transformation, global governance has come to a new crossroads. Against this backdrop, Xi put forward the Global Governance Initiative (GGI) at the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) summit in September 2025 in China's coastal city of Tianjin. "I look forward to working with all countries for a more just and equitable global governance system and advancing toward a community with a shared future for humanity," Xi said, stressing sovereign equality and genuine multilateralism. TRAFFIC LIGHTS "A world without rules is like a crossroads without traffic lights, where chaos and disorder are all but guaranteed," Xi said at the 2026 BRICS Summit in New Delhi, India. This metaphor highlights the importance of rules in maintaining the international order. While having rules in place matters, how they are made and who gets to make them matter even more. International rules must be written and upheld jointly by all countries based on the purposes and principles of the UN Charter, rather than dictated by those with the strongest muscles or the loudest voice, Xi once stressed. He has also called for the purposes and principles of the UN Charter and other universally recognized basic norms of international relations to be observed comprehensively, fully and in their entirety. "There should be no double standards, and the house rules of a few countries must not be imposed upon others," he said. The GGI proposed by President Xi reflects the objective transformation of the world system and responds to the aspirations of most countries for a fairer and more representative system of global governance, said Rahmon Ulmasov, a professor at the Russian-Tajik (Slavonic) University. MAKING THE PIE BIGGER Xi has repeatedly used the metaphor of a pie to describe the gains of international cooperation. "We should make the pie of win-win cooperation bigger, and ensure that more development gains will be shared more fairly by people across the world," he said at the 23rd meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization in 2023. The pie metaphor reflects the people-centered and action-oriented vision of the GGI: making the gains of cooperation bigger while ensuring that they are shared more widely and fairly. When proposing the GGI, Xi emphasized the importance of "ensuring that the people of every nation are the actors in and beneficiaries of global governance." The SCO, the platform where Xi proposed the GGI, provides an example. Within the grouping, China has announced the establishment of cooperation platforms in energy, green industries and the digital economy, as well as centers for scientific and technological innovation, higher education, and vocational and technical education. The expanding scope of cooperation shows how the "pie" can be made bigger in practice: by opening up new areas of cooperation, creating more opportunities for development and ensuring that the benefits reach more people. Beyond making the pie bigger, Xi has also called for sharing the pie fairly to ensure justice and equity. For him, the ultimate purpose of better global governance is to promote common development and improve people's well-being across the globe. At the G20 summit held in Brazil in 2024, Xi called for building a just world of common development, saying "prosperity and stability would not be possible in a world where the rich become richer while the poor are made poorer, and countries should make global development more inclusive, beneficial to all, and more resilient." To build such a world, Xi said, there should be more bridges of cooperation, and less "small yard, high fences," so that more and more developing countries will be better off and achieve modernization. ■

item.title: Xinhua Commentary: Global governance must keep pace with a changing world
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-23
BEIJING, Oct. 23 (Xinhua) -- Global governance must evolve to reflect the realities of today's world and respond more effectively to the needs of all countries, especially developing ones. As the 2026 Global Governance Forum (Xiongan) convenes, China's Global Governance Initiative (GGI) offers a timely framework for addressing this challenge through reform and improvement of the existing system. The need for change is growing ever more urgent. Development gaps remain wide, inequalities persist, and challenges ranging from climate change to debt distress continue to weigh heavily on developing countries. Yet, the current international institutions and global governance mechanisms tasked with addressing these issues do not always adequately reflect the changing distribution of global economic strength or give all countries an equal voice in making decisions that affect them. At the core of the current strain on the system lies a glaring representation gap. While emerging economies have become increasingly important drivers of global growth, their representation in some key decision-making bodies remains inadequate. As the global economic and demographic center of gravity shifts, this disparity is becoming difficult to ignore. The Global South should not remain a passive recipient of rules shaped by others. It must have a greater say in setting the global agenda and shaping international rules. Improving the representation of developing countries in global governance institutions is not a concession by the West, but a necessary adjustment to make the system more inclusive, representative and effective. Such reform would benefit the international community as a whole. The world is a single ship carrying all nations; its stability depends on their ability to meet shared challenges together. A governance system that fails to accommodate the legitimate concerns of a large part of the world will struggle to muster the collective response that global challenges require. Fairer representation, however, is only part of the answer. Global governance must also be judged by whether it improves people's wellbeing and delivers tangible results. International cooperation should serve ordinary people, and commitments made at the global level must translate into practical progress on the ground. These principles are central to the GGI, which sets out five core concepts: adhering to sovereign equality, abiding by the international rule of law, practicing multilateralism, advocating a people-centered approach, and focusing on taking real actions. The Initiative has gained support from nearly 160 countries and international organizations, while more than 60 countries have joined the Group of Friends of Global Governance. At its core, the GGI calls for global governance to keep pace with changing times while upholding the purposes and principles of the UN Charter. It seeks to reform and improve the existing global governance system, rather than to overturn the international order. The objective is to make multilateral institutions more responsive to today's challenges and better equipped to deliver results for the international community. This distinction matters. Reforming global governance is not a zero-sum game in which a greater role for the Global South must come at the expense of other countries. Nor is it about replacing one set of rules with another. It is about making international institutions more representative of the world as it is today, while strengthening the common rules and cooperation needed to address shared challenges. At a time when the world faces mounting uncertainties and increasingly interconnected challenges, the task is not simply to discuss what needs to change, but to build greater consensus on how to make global governance more inclusive, effective and action-oriented. By giving all countries a greater voice, putting people at the center and turning commitments into concrete results, the global community can build a system tailored to better meet challenges of our time. ■

item.title: China's innovation gains pace, powering new growth drivers: report
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-23
BEIJING, Oct. 23 (Xinhua) -- China's innovation capacity continued to strengthen last year, with the innovation environment improving and new growth drivers expanding, providing solid support for high-quality development, official data showed on Friday. The country's innovation index stood at 185.5 in 2025, up 6.4 percent from a year earlier, according to an annual report released by the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS). The sub-indices measuring the innovation environment, input, output and impact all kept rising last year. The report noted that multiple indicators performed well, including the share of science and technology appropriations in government budget spending, business R&D spending as a share of operating revenue, R&D spending as a share of GDP, the number of high-value invention patents per 10,000 R&D personnel, overall labor productivity, and high-tech products' share of goods exports. In China, innovation is gathering pace across the board. From DeepSeek's global splash to humanoid robots that wowed audiences, China's scientific achievements have been translating rapidly into industrial applications. Artificial intelligence (AI), new energy and new materials are among the sectors maintaining strong growth momentum. In the first three quarters of 2026, new drivers of growth, represented by high-end manufacturing, the digital and intelligent economy, and modern services, contributed more than 40 percent of China's economic growth. "The rapid growth of new drivers is a standout feature of this year's economic performance," Mao Shengyong, an NBS spokesperson, said. Separately, tax invoice data released by the State Taxation Administration on Friday also revealed that industries tied to new growth drivers have expanded faster this year, with those related to AI picking up speed especially quickly. In the third quarter of 2026, sales revenue of core industries of the digital economy, and patent-intensive industries rose 9.9 percent and 14.4 percent year on year, respectively, a clear acceleration from the second quarter, the tax data showed. Sales in the integrated circuits and semiconductor equipment manufacturing sectors surged 77.9 percent and 35.9 percent, respectively, from a year earlier. Innovation has long held an important place in China's development strategy. The latest major step comes as the guidelines on developing new quality productive forces were released earlier this month, spelling out the overall goals and key tasks for the 2026-2030 period. As China actively cultivates future industries, expands emerging sectors and upgrades traditional ones, the momentum built through innovation is steadily converting into economic growth, experts said. ■

item.title: Xi orders all-out rescue efforts after 7.0-magnitude earthquake in Xizang
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-23
BEIJING, Oct. 23 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has ordered all-out search and rescue efforts for the missing and prompt medical treatment for the injured after a 7.0-magnitude earthquake struck a county in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region on Thursday night. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, urged in an important instruction every effort to minimize casualties. The earthquake struck Baqen County in Nagqu City, Xizang, at 10:33 p.m. Thursday. The quake has left 16 people dead and 65 injured, according to local authorities. Noting that the affected area is at a high altitude with low temperatures, Xi stressed the need to closely monitor seismic activity and weather conditions to prevent secondary disasters. Efforts should be made to properly accommodate the affected residents, repair damaged infrastructure as quickly as possible, and safeguard people's lives and property, Xi said. Premier Li Qiang, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, called for solid disaster prevention and response efforts. The Ministry of Emergency Management and authorities in Xizang have mobilized resources for rescue and relief operations. ■

item.title: Xi chairs CPC leadership meeting to review disciplinary inspection report
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-23
BEIJING, Oct. 23 (Xinhua) -- The Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee held a meeting on Friday to review a report on the seventh round of disciplinary inspection launched by the 20th CPC Central Committee. Xi Jinping, general secretary of the CPC Central Committee, chaired the meeting. The meeting hailed the work performance and results of the inspection. According to the inspection results, central Party and government departments have made progress in their work, but some problems still exist and need to be taken seriously. The meeting urged solid efforts to rectify the problems identified by the inspection. It called on central Party and government departments to strengthen their sense of political responsibility in performing their duties, deepen reform, and ensure both development and security. It also stressed the need to strengthen leadership teams, while adopting higher standards and taking more concrete measures to advance full and rigorous Party self-governance. The meeting also discussed other matters. ■

item.title: "China Haul" reflects growing appeal of shopping in China
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-22
BEIJING, Oct. 22 (Xinhua) -- China's commerce ministry said that the "China Haul" trend on overseas social media reflects the rising recognition and appreciation of "Shopping in China." Yang Mu, head of the market operation and consumption promotion department of the Ministry of Commerce, said the phenomenon, depicting foreigners who share their experiences and joy of shopping in China on overseas social platforms, has also been a result of China's high-standard opening up and the charm of fine traditional Chinese culture. While commenting on booming inbound consumption at a press conference on Thursday, Yang said product categories favored by overseas consumers are expanding from traditional specialties such as tea and silk, previously the dominant choices, to tech gadgets, Chinese-style wellness products, beauty products and trendy toys. Shopping has become an important purpose of travel alongside sightseeing for overseas visitors, Yang said, adding that foreign visitors are now visiting more diverse corners of the country in addition to major cities. China continued to attract more foreign visitors in the third quarter of 2026, with visa-free entries rising 24.1 percent year on year to nearly 9 million. Visa-free entries accounted for 77.5 percent of all entries by foreign nationals during the period, official data showed. Building on the country's continued expansion of visa-free arrangements, a series of policy measures have also been rolled out to make shopping in China easier, including upgraded tax refund policies. From January to August this year, nationwide departure tax refund sales increased by about 60 percent year on year, and the number of people receiving tax refunds rose by 300 percent. At present, there are more than 18,000 tax refund stores nationwide, an increase of 400 percent compared with the end of 2024, official data showed. Yang said that going forward, the ministry will work to improve the "Shopping in China" experience by enriching high-quality supply, expanding the coverage of departure tax refunds, and improving payment-related services. ■

item.title: Xi calls for new achievements on new Long March
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-22
Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, delivers an important speech during a gathering commemorating the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Red Army's Long March held at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 22, 2026. (Xinhua/Yao Dawei) BEIJING, Oct. 22 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday called for new achievements on the new Long March as China commemorates the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Red Army's Long March. "Only by remembering history can we create a brighter future," said Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, when addressing a gathering held in Beijing to mark the anniversary. Under Xi's proposal, all participants stood up and observed a moment of silence for the revolutionary heroes who gave their lives during the Long March and in revolutionary struggles across China. From October 1934 to October 1936, the Red Army marched through more than 10 provinces during the Long March, opening up a new chapter in the Chinese revolution, Xi said. "This earth-shattering revolutionary feat holds great significance in the history of our Party, country and military, and has a profound impact on our path toward the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation," he noted. Xi stressed that the Party's right leadership and the establishment of Mao Zedong's core position were decisive for the victory of the Red Army's Long March. The Party and the Red Army relied on firm conviction, Xi said, adding that troops with noble ideals and firm beliefs are invincible. Xi emphasized the importance of integrating the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities in addressing the country's issues and problems. He further underscored that the people will always be the source of strength and a strong support for the Party and the people's armed forces. Xi said the great spirit of the Long March demonstrates the power of loyalty, truth, justice and unity. "It will always be a precious treasure and a powerful driving force inspiring us to overcome difficulties and forge ahead courageously." He said the road of the Long March continues to extend. "On our new journey, we are now committed to realizing the Second Centenary Goal of building China into a great modern socialist country in all respects and advancing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation on all fronts through a Chinese path to modernization," he said. To forge ahead on the new Long March, Xi said, it is imperative to stay committed to the Party's ideals, convictions and purpose and rely closely on the people to create new achievements. He underscored the need to unswervingly advance high-quality development and promote common prosperity for all. Efforts must be made to better ensure both development and security and seize the historical initiative to overcome difficulties, combat risks and meet challenges, he stressed. Xi also emphasized the importance of moving more quickly to reinforce the people's armed forces to world-class standards and adhering to the Party's absolute leadership over the military. It is also vital to uphold the leadership of the Party, strengthen Party building and persevere with full and rigorous Party self-governance, he added. Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi, who are members of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, as well as Chinese Vice President Han Zheng, attended the gathering. Zhao, who presided over the event, said Xi's speech was of immense political, ideological and guiding significance, urging earnest efforts to study and grasp its essence and ensure its effective implementation. He called on the whole Party, the entire military and the Chinese people of all ethnic groups to rally more closely around the Party Central Committee with Xi at its core and strive to build a great country and advance national rejuvenation on all fronts through Chinese modernization. Around 3,000 people participated in the gathering at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing. ■ A gathering commemorating the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Red Army's Long March is held at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 22, 2026.
